title: estoy para ti / por ti, por for exchanges, 'to' form after prepositions, false friends

cards.title: Estoy para ti = I'm there for you
cards.body: Estar already implies location, so no 'there' is needed. Knocking on a door or messaging: ¿Estás? On the phone: ¿Está Juan?

examples.es: Estoy por ti. / Estoy por usted.

examples.en: It's because of you that we've come.
examples.es: Es por ti que hemos venido.

examples.en: I'd change this one for that one.
Why wouldn't you swap these for those?
examples.es: ¿Por qué no cambiarías estas por esas?

cards.title: x = por
cards.body: Por is also 'times' in maths (ocho por ocho), so online you may see x for por: gracias x venir. Careful if you sign off with kisses as x!

cards.title: After prepositions: the 'to' form, not -ing
cards.body: English says 'thanks for calling'; Spanish uses the 'to' form after para, por, de, en, con, a.

examples.en: It's a way of doing it.

cards.title: creer = to believe; creo (two meanings)
cards.body: Creo is both 'I believe' (creer) and 'I create' (crear).

cards.title: False friends: discutir, actual
cards.body: Discutir usually means 'to argue' (argüir is to argue a point). Actual means 'current' and actualmente 'currently'. Most Latin conversions are reliable, but watch for these.

examples.en: I don't believe in arguing like this.
examples.es: No creo en discutir de esta forma.
